PC: Perform a rapid assessment: CAB, vital signs
Perform a focused history and examination
Request appropriate tests: Lab, EKG, Chest x-ray, ABG
Early cardiovascular support with initiation of IV fluids
Place the patient on cardiac monitor
Treatment of the seizure with benzodiazepines first, then treatment of refractory seizures with IV propofol or phenobarbital
Gastrointestinal decontamination with activated charcoal once vomiting controlled
Cautious correction of hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia and hyperglycemia
MK: Identification of the causative agent: Theophylline poisoning
Recognize that if sedative meds are given, respiratory support with endotracheal intubation is indicated
SBP: Request appropriate consults: Toxicology, Nephrology and Critical Care
